amendments.because: Forge's own forge.toml can only take fast_test once the installed Forge is a release that knows it; that line moves to a follow-up after the next release
amendments.done_when: When forge init or adoption sets a repo's test command, it also sets fast_test to a changed-only command for the repo's test tool when it recognises one (vitest: vitest related or --changed {base}; jest: --changedSince {base}; pytest: the test files that changed since {base} plus those that import a changed module), and leaves it unset otherwise; the skill tells the agent to propose one when a repo has none. Forge's own forge.toml sets fast_test the same way for its pytest suite. Command-level tests cover init in a vitest repo, a jest repo, a pytest repo and an unknown one.

findings.body: The coordinator deferred Forge's own configuration to a later release, but this test still indexes `own["fast_test"]`. The new evidence is that the amended requirement excludes this setting while the test remains unchanged. Reading `forge.toml:6–8` confirms the key is absent, so this collected test raises `KeyError` and prevents the repository suite from passing. Move this test to the deferred work rather than adding the ruled-out configuration.
findings.title: Remove the obsolete test requiring Forge's own fast_test setting

findings.body: The previous finding remains open: everything after `pytest` is discarded, including shell delimiters. Adoption with `--test '(cd backend && pytest tests)'` generates `(cd backend && python -c "…"` without the closing parenthesis. `src/forge/review.py:283` executes this through a shell, so close fails before running tests. Preserve enclosing shell syntax when replacing the pytest invocation.
findings.title: Preserve enclosing shell syntax when replacing pytest

findings.body: The previous finding remains open. With rename detection enabled, `--name-only` reports the post-image filename, as specified by the [Git documentation](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-diff#Documentation/git-diff.txt---name-only). Renaming `shop/orders.py` to `shop/purchases.py` therefore selects importers of `purchases` but misses unchanged tests importing `shop.orders`. A rename-only change can return success without exposing those broken imports. Include both names or disable rename detection for this list.
findings.title: Include the old module name when selecting tests for renames

findings.body: For adoption with `--test 'cd backend && pytest tests'`, the selector runs inside `backend`. `git diff --name-only` supplies `backend/tests/test_orders.py`, while `git ls-files` supplies `tests/test_orders.py`; their default path conventions differ, as documented for [diff](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-diff#Documentation/git-diff.txt---relativepath) and [ls-files](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-ls-files#Documentation/git-ls-files.txt---full-name). If only that test changed, `names` is empty and this comparison omits it, returning success without running it. Normalize both lists, for example by using `git diff --relative`.
findings.title: Compare changed test paths relative to the same directory

findings.body: The import expression only searches one line. An unchanged test containing `from shop import (\n    orders,\n)` imports `shop.orders`, but changing `shop/orders.py` does not select it: the `from` line contains no `orders`, and the following line contains no `from` or `import`. Close can consequently report that no tests ran despite a direct importer being present. Recognize complete import statements rather than individual lines.
findings.title: Recognize changed modules in multiline imports

why: Repos only get change-based test runs at close if someone sets fast_test by hand, so most closes still run the full suite that CI runs again
